boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Roan's Tan Yard (Silver Creek) record (January 8, 1862) in Operations in Northeast Missouri [December 1861]. The reconnaissances of January 5-7 and the return march are context; the frozen record falls after the campaign's December 1861 label. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives the Union detachments 450 and the Confederates unknown; the live field reads US 450 and CS 0. Torrence says 500 mounted men went out and that Poindexter's camp held 600 (read 'COO' in OCR) to 800 enlisted men and as many sympathizers. Turner, relaying Hubbard, says the rebels were 900 strong.
claims.rationale: Column figures and estimates of the enemy relayed at second hand; no return. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live CS zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Colonel J. A. Poindexter and Major W. M. G. Torrence. Torrence says he was joined by Hunt's companies of Merrill's Horse and Hubbard's four companies of the First Missouri, assigned Hunt the carbine companies and ordered the First Iowa charge. Turner's report, from Hubbard, credits Hubbard with the attack and the rout.
claims.rationale: Two interested accounts credit different majors; no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text and the live field read 91 (US 11; CS 80). Torrence says the enemy's killed and wounded could not be less than 80 to 100 and gives no Union figure. Turner, from Hubbard, gives the enemy's loss as 40 killed and 60 wounded and Hubbard's as 6 killed and 19 wounded, with 28 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Hubbard's figures may cover only his own command.

open_questions: Palmer's No. 1 and Merrill's No. 4 reports (printed with Torrence's and Turner's; read while delimiting, not selected), Hubbard's own report, the Confederate side, returns and maps remain deferred. Britton's volume does not name the action; no nineteenth-century history was selected.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Torrence's January 10, 1862 report is an interested Union account. Turner's January 14, 1862 report relays Major Hubbard's account at second hand and is a separate family. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
